newsitem.title: UK: Fresh clues on 'new Pearson' sought at H1.
newsitem.headline: Fresh clues on 'new Pearson' sought at H1.

text.p: Analysts will seek fresh clues on the future strategy of diversified UK media and leisure group Pearson Plc when it publishes interim results on Monday.

Pre-tax profits are expected to total 43-48 million stg for Pearson, a company which earns most of its profits in the second half of the year. Last year's interim figures were complicated by several exceptional items but most analysts are using a comparative figure of 39.8 million stg.
Interim dividend is forecast to increase to 7.48-7.6p from 6.9p at this stage in 1996.
Pearson chief executive Marjorie Scardino, who took office in January, has vowed to improve the financial performance of the business and promised "evolution not revolution".
She said at the time of full-year results in March that it was not possible for her to sweep in and unveil a 'new Pearson' but analysts are hoping she can bring greater focus to the group.
Scardino and her team needed to devote management time to the effects of an accounting scam at the company's Penguin USA book subsidiary which could cost the company up to 100 million stg.
That 100 million stg provision was taken in last year's accounts but Pearson has said there could be a one-off delay in cash collection from its major North American customers.
The strength of sterling was also likely to depress earnings as will start-up costs from the new Channel 5 UK television channel, in which Pearson is one of four shareholders.

Rumours of a rift between Scardino and Pearson Television boss Greg Dyke also surfaced recently in the British press. Dyke was believed to want to lead a management buy-out of the TV arm but Scardino was reported to have vetoed the plan.
